Let $U=\{l,m,n,o\}$ be the universal set and let $K=\{l,m,o\}.$ What is $\overset{―}{K}?$" :question/worked-solution "The complement of $K,$ denoted $\overset{―}{K},$ consists of all the elements in $U$ that are not in $K.$ To represent $\overset{―}{K},$ we will shade in all the area of $U$ that is *outside* of $K,$ as follows:

![](images/74/74345aeb2a1028e07d155dd357a9bb412860309c99cee37c62380907b3e1bd37.png)

The element in the shaded area is $n.$ This is the only element of $U$ that is not in $K.$ Therefore, the complement of $K$ is

$$
\overset{―}{K}=\{n\}.
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186237670 :answer-field/correct "answer-79ed194c-0f65-59da-943b-f2c0c42ad0b9" :answer-field/choices ["answer-4a9cf07e-f5b9-520a-9ad5-197f7e218f70" "answer-64bd11a0-bdcc-5e85-b42d-a6873a171fc8" "answer-39957d77-14fe-5afa-b55e-fc5c5516d904" "answer-514f2e88-12df-5701-b9d7-b5ac210719ae" "answer-79ed194c-0f65-59da-943b-f2c0c42ad0b9"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-4a9cf07e-f5b9-520a-9ad5-197f7e218f70" :answer/id #uuid "4a9cf07e-f5b9-520a-9ad5-197f7e218f70" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{l,m,n,o\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-64bd11a0-bdcc-5e85-b42d-a6873a171fc8" :answer/id #uuid "64bd11a0-bdcc-5e85-b42d-a6873a171fc8" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{l,m,n\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-39957d77-14fe-5afa-b55e-fc5c5516d904" :answer/id #uuid "39957d77-14fe-5afa-b55e-fc5c5516d904" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{m,n\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-514f2e88-12df-5701-b9d7-b5ac210719ae" :answer/id #uuid "514f2e88-12df-5701-b9d7-b5ac210719ae" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{m\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-79ed194c-0f65-59da-943b-f2c0c42ad0b9" :answer/id #uuid "79ed194c-0f65-59da-943b-f2c0c42ad0b9" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{n\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186240999 :question/problem "If $U=\{2,4,6,8,…,20\}$ is the universal set and $B=\{4,8,12,16,20\},$ then the complement of $B$ is" :question/worked-solution "The complement of $B,$ denoted $\overset{―}{B},$ consists of every element in the universal set $U$ that is not in the set $B.$

The elements of $U$ that are not in $B$ are $2,$ $6,$ $10,$ $14,$ and $18.$

Therefore, the complement of $B$ is

$$
\overset{―}{B}=\{2,6,10,14,18\}.
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186240345 :answer-field/correct "answer-9a07857f-9b04-5e82-82b2-f3b3a50169ba" :answer-field/choices ["answer-590e2e96-c4ed-5c5c-bd74-ac6935a254f4" "answer-9a07857f-9b04-5e82-82b2-f3b3a50169ba" "answer-30e9f955-9c5f-5995-8b92-02a7c9a66c34" "answer-092d96cc-31d1-57b6-b25f-cb1f645761fb" "answer-dc7d8ee0-c616-5f34-81ae-9932e04e4685"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-590e2e96-c4ed-5c5c-bd74-ac6935a254f4" :answer/id #uuid "590e2e96-c4ed-5c5c-bd74-ac6935a254f4" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{0,2,6,10,14,18\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-9a07857f-9b04-5e82-82b2-f3b3a50169ba" :answer/id #uuid "9a07857f-9b04-5e82-82b2-f3b3a50169ba" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{2,6,10,14,18\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-30e9f955-9c5f-5995-8b92-02a7c9a66c34" :answer/id #uuid "30e9f955-9c5f-5995-8b92-02a7c9a66c34" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{2,6,10,14\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-092d96cc-31d1-57b6-b25f-cb1f645761fb" :answer/id #uuid "092d96cc-31d1-57b6-b25f-cb1f645761fb" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{2,6,10,18\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-dc7d8ee0-c616-5f34-81ae-9932e04e4685" :answer/id #uuid "dc7d8ee0-c616-5f34-81ae-9932e04e4685" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{6,10,14,18\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186241005 :question/problem "Let $U=\{a,b,c,…,z\}$ be the universal set and $Y=\{a,b,c,…,j\}$, then $\overset{―}{Y}=$" :question/worked-solution "The complement of $Y,$ denoted $\overset{―}{Y},$ consists of every element in the universal set $U$ that is not in the set $Y.$

The universal set $U$ consists of the letters $a$ through $z,$ while the set $Y$ consists of the letters $a$ through $j.$

So, the only elements of $U$ that are not in $Y$ are the letters $k$ through $z.$

Therefore, the complement of $Y$ is

$$
\overset{―}{Y}=\{k,l,m,…,z\}.
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186240596 :answer-field/correct "answer-7c72eb67-dc8d-5199-baad-e8806a1db03d" :answer-field/choices ["answer-3b4fe627-d7c1-50a5-a27e-4f77766ccffc" "answer-1bf1ba90-d97e-56e1-8be0-67555fe8bfec" "answer-7c72eb67-dc8d-5199-baad-e8806a1db03d" "answer-d249a876-1cdc-59b3-9cf5-a76a41e27fb1" "answer-84ffc0a6-3416-5aad-a60b-0475613c9718"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3b4fe627-d7c1-50a5-a27e-4f77766ccffc" :answer/id #uuid "3b4fe627-d7c1-50a5-a27e-4f77766ccffc" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{i,j,k,…,z\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1bf1ba90-d97e-56e1-8be0-67555fe8bfec" :answer/id #uuid "1bf1ba90-d97e-56e1-8be0-67555fe8bfec" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{j,k,l…,z\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-7c72eb67-dc8d-5199-baad-e8806a1db03d" :answer/id #uuid "7c72eb67-dc8d-5199-baad-e8806a1db03d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{k,l,m,…,z\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-d249a876-1cdc-59b3-9cf5-a76a41e27fb1" :answer/id #uuid "d249a876-1cdc-59b3-9cf5-a76a41e27fb1" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{l,m,n…,z\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-84ffc0a6-3416-5aad-a60b-0475613c9718" :answer/id #uuid "84ffc0a6-3416-5aad-a60b-0475613c9718" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{m,n,o…,z\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186399685 :question/worked-solution "Consider the line $x+2y=-8.$ Since the line is solid, the inequality is an "or equal to" inequality. Writing the equation of this line in slope-intercept form, we have

$$
y=-\frac{1}{2}x-4.
$$

Now, since the shaded region lies *above* the line, the inequality is a "greater than" inequality. So the corresponding inequality is

$$
y\ge -\frac{1}{2}x-4,
$$

    

which we can rewrite as

$$
x+2y\ge -8.
$$

Now consider the line $y=\frac{1}{2}x+1.$ Since the line is solid, the inequality is an "or equal to" inequality. Also, since the shaded region lies *below* the line, the inequality is a "less than" inequality. So the corresponding inequality is

$$
y\le \frac{1}{2}x+1.
$$

Therefore, the system of inequalities that defines the shaded region is

$$

$$
f(x)=(x+2)^{4}(x+5)(x-7).
$$

So we're now solving the inequality $f(x)\ge 0.$

The solutions to the equation $f(x)=0$ are $x=-5,$ $x=-2,$ and $x=7.$ These roots divide the number line into $4$ subintervals:

$$
(-\infty ,-5),\,(-5,-2),\,(-2,7),\,(7,\infty ).
$$

Now, we construct a sign table with the list of the intervals on the top and the list of factors on the left. Filling in the sign table using the usual method, we get the following result:

|  | $(-\infty ,-5)$ | $(-5,-2)$ | $(-2,7)$ | $(7,\infty )$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $(x+2)^{4}$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| $x+5$ | $-$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| $x-7$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| $f(x)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |

Finally, to solve the inequality $f(x)\ge 0,$ we look at the bottom row to determine where $f(x)$ is positive.

From the table, we see that $f(x)$ is positive on the intervals $(-\infty ,-5)$ and $(7,\infty ).$

Therefore, remembering that the roots are also solutions, we conclude that $f(x)\ge 0$ for all $x\in (-\infty ,-5]\cup \{-2\}\cup [7,\infty ).$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186252925 :answer-field/correct "answer-54ce1c89-ead7-51f7-8d45-c8b886b66b84" :answer-field/choices ["answer-54ce1c89-ead7-51f7-8d45-c8b886b66b84" "answer-4c47f54b-e89e-5b4f-8218-dda45e7ee776"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-54ce1c89-ead7-51f7-8d45-c8b886b66b84" :answer/id #uuid "54ce1c89-ead7-51f7-8d45-c8b886b66b84" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "x\in (-\infty ,-5]\cup \{-2\}\cup [7,\infty )" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-4c47f54b-e89e-5b4f-8218-dda45e7ee776" :answer/id #uuid "4c47f54b-e89e-5b4f-8218-dda45e7ee776" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "x\in \{-2\}\cup [7,\infty )" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186253275 :question/worked-solution "First, we factor the polynomial on the left-hand side of the inequality:

$$

The solutions to the equation $f(x)=0$ are $x=-7,$ $x=0,$ and $x=4.$ These roots divide the number line into $4$ subintervals: 

$$

$$

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x+7$ | $-$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| ${x}^{2}$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| $x-4$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| $f(x)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |

Finally, to solve the inequality $f(x)\ge 0,$ we look at the bottom row to determine where $f(x)$ is positive.

From the table, we see that $f(x)$ is positive on the intervals $(-\infty ,-7),$ and $(4,\infty ).$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ Therefore, the parametric equations are:

$$

$$

Comparing the above to our given equation

$$
\frac{x-10}{7}=\frac{y-(-8)}{-4}=\frac{z-(-1)}{11},
$$

$$

$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=1 \\ {x}_{2}=1 \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=7\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 5 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-5{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=1 \\ {x}_{2}=1 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=1.$ Substituting into the first equation gives 

$$
{x}_{1}-1=1\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2.
$$

Since the system has a solution, we can conclude that $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}.$

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $b$ as a linear combination of ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}:$

$$

$$

$$

$$" :question/worked-solution "To find $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{1}),$ we need to find the number that is located in row $3$ and position $1$ of Pascal's triangle. 

**Important**: When counting the rows and positions in Pascal's triangle, we always start counting from zero! Remember:

- The top row of Pascal's triangle is row $0.$

- The first position of each row (the one of the left) is position number $0.$

The location of $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{1})$ in Pascal's triangle is highlighted below.

$$
\begin{aligned} &  &  &  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{0}{0}) \\  &  &  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{1}{0}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{1}{1}) \\  &  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{0}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{1}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{2}) \\  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{0}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{1}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{2}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{3}) \\  &  &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Now, $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{1})$ is the sum of the two closest numbers located in the previous row. So,

$$

$$" :question/worked-solution "To find $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{2}),$ we need to find the number that is located in row $3$ and position $2$ of Pascal's triangle. 

**Important**: When counting the rows and positions in Pascal's triangle, we always start counting from zero! Remember:

- The top row of Pascal's triangle is row $0.$

- The first position of each row (the one of the left) is position number $0.$

The location of $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{2})$ in Pascal's triangle is highlighted below.

$$
\begin{aligned} &  &  &  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{0}{0}) \\  &  &  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{1}{0}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{1}{1}) \\  &  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{0}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{1}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{2}) \\  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{0}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{1}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{2}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{3}) \\  &  &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Now, $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{2})$ is the sum of the two closest numbers located in the previous row. So,

$$
(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{2})=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{1})+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{2})
$$

Therefore, the missing expression is $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{2}).$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186335645 :answer-field/correct "answer-4f61bb02-7c6b-599e-bcda-28faca2378f8" :answer-field/choices ["answer-7b20281e-3116-5c7a-9362-f88b58a1e766" "answer-3d54b2a8-70b8-57d2-b26c-e1b263ac6824" "answer-809103a8-aba5-597f-b3d9-d4ff88026e05" "answer-a725e35f-5fa7-5d30-a593-8ae1d44e2785" "answer-4f61bb02-7c6b-599e-bcda-28faca2378f8"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-7b20281e-3116-5c7a-9362-f88b58a1e766" :answer/id #uuid "7b20281e-3116-5c7a-9362-f88b58a1e766" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{1}{0})" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3d54b2a8-70b8-57d2-b26c-e1b263ac6824" :answer/id #uuid "3d54b2a8-70b8-57d2-b26c-e1b263ac6824" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{1}{1})" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-809103a8-aba5-597f-b3d9-d4ff88026e05" :answer/id #uuid "809103a8-aba5-597f-b3d9-d4ff88026e05" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{0})" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a725e35f-5fa7-5d30-a593-8ae1d44e2785" :answer/id #uuid "a725e35f-5fa7-5d30-a593-8ae1d44e2785" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{1})" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-4f61bb02-7c6b-599e-bcda-28faca2378f8" :answer/id #uuid "4f61bb02-7c6b-599e-bcda-28faca2378f8" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{2})" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186338838 :question/worked-solution "Remember that the Cartesian (canonical) equation of the straight line that passes through the point $P({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=⟨{v}_{x},{v}_{y},{v}_{z}⟩$, is given by

$$
\frac{x-{x}_{0}}{{v}_{x}}=\frac{y-{y}_{0}}{{v}_{y}}=\frac{z-{z}_{0}}{{v}_{z}}=t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Comparing the above to our given equation

$$
\frac{x-11}{-4}=\frac{y-(-3)}{5}=\frac{z-(-1)}{3},
$$

we find that our line passes through the point $P(11,-3,-1)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨-4,5,3⟩.$ Therefore, its vector equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ -3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations are the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=11-4t \\ y=-3+5t \\ z=-1+3t\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186338687 :answer-field/correct "answer-4b7409a3-17df-5f35-9a98-53b2b56e27b0" :answer-field/choices ["answer-2aad0314-cdde-56d6-9fc9-f1e44fdcf531" "answer-2670e300-5558-54cf-aa24-1fbeb9d684b0" "answer-b720935d-3a6b-53b7-8467-e0328c75249f" "answer-4b7409a3-17df-5f35-9a98-53b2b56e27b0"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-2aad0314-cdde-56d6-9fc9-f1e44fdcf531" :answer/id #uuid "2aad0314-cdde-56d6-9fc9-f1e44fdcf531" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}x=-11-4t \\ y=3+5t \\ z=1+3t\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-2670e300-5558-54cf-aa24-1fbeb9d684b0" :answer/id #uuid "2670e300-5558-54cf-aa24-1fbeb9d684b0" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}x=-4+11t \\ y=5-3t \\ z=3-t\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b720935d-3a6b-53b7-8467-e0328c75249f" :answer/id #uuid "b720935d-3a6b-53b7-8467-e0328c75249f" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}x=-4t \\ y=5t \\ z=3t\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-4b7409a3-17df-5f35-9a98-53b2b56e27b0" :answer/id #uuid "4b7409a3-17df-5f35-9a98-53b2b56e27b0" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}x=11-4t \\ y=-3+5t \\ z=-1+3t\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186351158 :question/problem "Find all of the subsets of $U=\{-\pi ,\pi \}.$" :question/worked-solution "To find every subset of $U,$ we list out every combination of elements within $U.$ 

We can use the following diagram to visualize the process:

Note that we must include the empty set since it is a subset of every set.

By doing this, we get

$$
∅,\{-\pi \},\{\pi \},\{-\pi ,\pi \}.
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186351128 :answer-field/correct "answer-a581296f-1ffd-5680-83b4-0a132fb259d4" :answer-field/choices ["answer-cceb7cd8-d3cb-5022-80c1-91cc18c492dd" "answer-a7e833ed-7b92-5b0e-ac1a-b54703f7a2bf" "answer-d6a266a0-5552-509f-ae6b-32ef2b01771f" "answer-8560767a-af4e-5ac9-984b-0d56ecc22cf9" "answer-a581296f-1ffd-5680-83b4-0a132fb259d4"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-cceb7cd8-d3cb-5022-80c1-91cc18c492dd" :answer/id #uuid "cceb7cd8-d3cb-5022-80c1-91cc18c492dd" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{-\pi \},\{\pi \}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a7e833ed-7b92-5b0e-ac1a-b54703f7a2bf" :answer/id #uuid "a7e833ed-7b92-5b0e-ac1a-b54703f7a2bf" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{-\pi \},\{\pi \},\{-\pi ,\pi \}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-d6a266a0-5552-509f-ae6b-32ef2b01771f" :answer/id #uuid "d6a266a0-5552-509f-ae6b-32ef2b01771f" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "∅,\{-\pi ,\pi \}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8560767a-af4e-5ac9-984b-0d56ecc22cf9" :answer/id #uuid "8560767a-af4e-5ac9-984b-0d56ecc22cf9" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "∅,\{-\pi \},\{\pi \}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a581296f-1ffd-5680-83b4-0a132fb259d4" :answer/id #uuid "a581296f-1ffd-5680-83b4-0a132fb259d4" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "∅,\{-\pi \},\{\pi \},\{-\pi ,\pi \}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186351176 :question/worked-solution "The multiples of $10$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
C=\{10,20,30,40,50,60,70,…\}.
$$

Likewise, multiples of $5$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
D=\{5,10,15,20,25,30,35,40,45,50,55,60,65,70,75,…\}.
$$

Now, $C∖D$ is the *difference* of $C$ and $D,$ which means that we want to find the elements that are in $C$ but *not* in $D.$

The elements of $C$ that are also in $D$ are $10,20,30,40,$ and so on (i.e. multiples of $10$). So, we must remove these elements from $C.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}C∖D & =C-D \\  & =\{10,20,30,40,50,60,70,…\}-\{5,10,15,20,25,30,35,40,45,50,55,60,65,70,75,…\} \\  & =∅.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186351004 :answer-field/choices ["answer-1eee49b7-7d23-57d3-be48-80546786725e" "answer-d54904e8-c3f4-50ab-b94b-312c9c80dbb1" "answer-3656c7be-564a-5dca-b523-f1cf8ca9939f" "answer-e8c1a6ce-e81b-50b5-825e-bab71ce12858"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1eee49b7-7d23-57d3-be48-80546786725e" :answer/id #uuid "1eee49b7-7d23-57d3-be48-80546786725e" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{10,20,30,40,50,60,70,…\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-d54904e8-c3f4-50ab-b94b-312c9c80dbb1" :answer/id #uuid "d54904e8-c3f4-50ab-b94b-312c9c80dbb1" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{15,30,45,60,75,…\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3656c7be-564a-5dca-b523-f1cf8ca9939f" :answer/id #uuid "3656c7be-564a-5dca-b523-f1cf8ca9939f" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{5,10,15,20,25,30,35,40,45,50,55,60,65,70,75,…\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-e8c1a6ce-e81b-50b5-825e-bab71ce12858" :answer/id #uuid "e8c1a6ce-e81b-50b5-825e-bab71ce12858" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{5,15,25,35,45,55,65,75,…\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186351258 :question/problem "If $U=\{1,2,3,…,10\}$ is the universal set and $A=\{2,4,6,8,10\},$ then the complement of $A$ is" :question/worked-solution "The complement of $A,$ denoted $\overset{―}{A},$ consists of every element in the universal set $U$ that is not in the set $A.$

\overset{―}{A}=\{1,3,5,7,9\}.
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186350765 :answer-field/correct "answer-32175474-2a33-5edd-82d1-ca23fe06b582" :answer-field/choices ["answer-8e2a7810-134a-59c6-95e0-9e32883d711d" "answer-5b05c18c-16d7-52fb-815b-13f340ae470d" "answer-32175474-2a33-5edd-82d1-ca23fe06b582" "answer-0ae8da4d-49d1-5d59-b5f2-9ba7fac1a5ce" "answer-62686a45-f9e0-5352-8bd0-280e32a4a7dd"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8e2a7810-134a-59c6-95e0-9e32883d711d" :answer/id #uuid "8e2a7810-134a-59c6-95e0-9e32883d711d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{0,3,6,9\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-5b05c18c-16d7-52fb-815b-13f340ae470d" :answer/id #uuid "5b05c18c-16d7-52fb-815b-13f340ae470d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-32175474-2a33-5edd-82d1-ca23fe06b582" :answer/id #uuid "32175474-2a33-5edd-82d1-ca23fe06b582" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{1,3,5,7,9\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-0ae8da4d-49d1-5d59-b5f2-9ba7fac1a5ce" :answer/id #uuid "0ae8da4d-49d1-5d59-b5f2-9ba7fac1a5ce" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{1,3,6,9\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-62686a45-f9e0-5352-8bd0-280e32a4a7dd" :answer/id #uuid "62686a45-f9e0-5352-8bd0-280e32a4a7dd" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{3,5,7,9\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186351259 :question/problem "If $U=\{-20,-18,-16,-14,…,20\}$ is the universal set and $A=\{-20,-16,-12,-8,…,20\},$ then $\overset{―}{A}=$" :question/worked-solution "The complement of $A,$ denoted $\overset{―}{A},$ consists of every element in the universal set $U$ that is not in the set $A.$

Given the sets $S=\{p,a,s,w,o,r,d\}$ and $T=\{p,o,r,t,e,l\},$ find $T∖S.$" :question/worked-solution "The difference $T∖S$ consists of all the elements that are in $T$ but not $S.$ To represent $T∖S,$ we will shade in all the area that is contained in $T$ but not $S.$

Therefore, the difference is

$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186350742 :answer-field/correct "answer-cde8a77d-917c-5d32-aebb-5d7a0c324a5d" :answer-field/choices ["answer-44d69e04-701b-532a-8660-e10b61e27da0" "answer-c0ebd0cd-50f3-5d9b-b33d-13fa3b3356f9" "answer-6386c1eb-6556-5007-86bd-5b23aac19731" "answer-3e57db84-9532-5a86-b209-39f3021ccc79" "answer-cde8a77d-917c-5d32-aebb-5d7a0c324a5d"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-44d69e04-701b-532a-8660-e10b61e27da0" :answer/id #uuid "44d69e04-701b-532a-8660-e10b61e27da0" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{a,s,w,d\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-c0ebd0cd-50f3-5d9b-b33d-13fa3b3356f9" :answer/id #uuid "c0ebd0cd-50f3-5d9b-b33d-13fa3b3356f9" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{p,a,s,t,e,l\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-6386c1eb-6556-5007-86bd-5b23aac19731" :answer/id #uuid "6386c1eb-6556-5007-86bd-5b23aac19731" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{p,o,r\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3e57db84-9532-5a86-b209-39f3021ccc79" :answer/id #uuid "3e57db84-9532-5a86-b209-39f3021ccc79" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{t,e,l,a,s,w,d\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-cde8a77d-917c-5d32-aebb-5d7a0c324a5d" :answer/id #uuid "cde8a77d-917c-5d32-aebb-5d7a0c324a5d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{t,e,l\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186351367 :question/worked-solution "The multiples of $3$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
A=\{3,6,9,12,15,18,21,24,…\}.
$$

Likewise, multiples of $4$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
B=\{4,8,12,16,20,24,…\}.
$$

Now, $B-A$ is the *difference* of $B$ and $A,$ which means that we want to find the elements that are in $B$ but *not* in $A.$

The elements of $B$ that are also in $A$ are $12,24,$ and so on (i.e. multiples of $12$). So, we must remove these elements from $B.$ Therefore, we have

Writing the equation of this line in slope-intercept form, we have

$$
y=-x+3.
$$

Now, since the shaded region lies *above* the line, the inequality is a "greater than"  inequality. So the corresponding inequality is

$$
y>-x+3,
$$

    

which we can rewrite as

$$
x+y>3.
$$

Now consider the line $y=2x.$ Since the line is dashed, the inequality is strict.  Also, since the shaded region lies *above* the line, the inequality is a "greater than" inequality. So the corresponding inequality is

$$
y>2x.
$$

Therefore, the system of inequalities that defines the shaded region is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+y>3 \\ y>2x.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186404462 :answer-field/correct "answer-27635777-a8dd-5afe-a296-ee402af7fe39" :answer-field/choices ["answer-7fa72215-7cb2-51f3-b5db-2adac83c439f" "answer-6f580ecb-7efc-5512-9398-273631dd1bd9" "answer-480417bf-3b78-555e-8194-c8ef38995e34" "answer-27635777-a8dd-5afe-a296-ee402af7fe39" "answer-b0260bc6-012f-5b9c-a80e-93287d27b6c3"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-7fa72215-7cb2-51f3-b5db-2adac83c439f" :answer/id #uuid "7fa72215-7cb2-51f3-b5db-2adac83c439f" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}x+y<3 \\ y<2x\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-6f580ecb-7efc-5512-9398-273631dd1bd9" :answer/id #uuid "6f580ecb-7efc-5512-9398-273631dd1bd9" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}x+y<3 \\ y>2x\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-480417bf-3b78-555e-8194-c8ef38995e34" :answer/id #uuid "480417bf-3b78-555e-8194-c8ef38995e34" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}x+y>3 \\ y<2x\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-27635777-a8dd-5afe-a296-ee402af7fe39" :answer/id #uuid "27635777-a8dd-5afe-a296-ee402af7fe39" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}x+y>3 \\ y>2x\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b0260bc6-012f-5b9c-a80e-93287d27b6c3" :answer/id #uuid "b0260bc6-012f-5b9c-a80e-93287d27b6c3" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}x+y\le 3 \\ y\ge 2x\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186404468 :question/worked-solution "Consider the line $y=4x+3.$ Since the line is dashed, the inequality is strict. Also, since the shaded region lies *below* the line, the inequality is a "less than" inequality. So the corresponding inequality is

$$
y<4x+3.
$$

    

Now consider the line $y=\frac{1}{4}x-2.$ Since the line is dashed, the inequality is strict. Also, since the shaded region lies *above* the line, the inequality is a "greater than" inequality. So the corresponding inequality is

$$
y>\frac{1}{4}x-2.
$$

Therefore, the system of inequalities that defines the shaded region is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}y<4x+3 \\ y>\frac{1}{4}x-2.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186404469 :answer-field/correct "answer-fbeae658-1ad6-5399-b8e3-d95d56f3c62b" :answer-field/choices ["answer-fbeae658-1ad6-5399-b8e3-d95d56f3c62b" "answer-8ff44b6f-7f18-5b59-b687-6bfafa9923c1" "answer-c6b98254-dc2c-5569-ba7c-775a46563922" "answer-21f1cf91-2163-5bf5-8bdd-17c06cfb56f3" "answer-49247309-afac-5793-a965-e29d26e684cb"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-fbeae658-1ad6-5399-b8e3-d95d56f3c62b" :answer/id #uuid "fbeae658-1ad6-5399-b8e3-d95d56f3c62b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}y<4x+3 \\ y>\frac{1}{4}x-2\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8ff44b6f-7f18-5b59-b687-6bfafa9923c1" :answer/id #uuid "8ff44b6f-7f18-5b59-b687-6bfafa9923c1" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}y>4x+3 \\ y<\frac{1}{4}x-2\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-c6b98254-dc2c-5569-ba7c-775a46563922" :answer/id #uuid "c6b98254-dc2c-5569-ba7c-775a46563922" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}y>4x+3 \\ y>\frac{1}{4}x-2\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-21f1cf91-2163-5bf5-8bdd-17c06cfb56f3" :answer/id #uuid "21f1cf91-2163-5bf5-8bdd-17c06cfb56f3" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}y>4x+3 \\ y\ge \frac{1}{4}x-2\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-49247309-afac-5793-a965-e29d26e684cb" :answer/id #uuid "49247309-afac-5793-a965-e29d26e684cb" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}y\le 4x+3 \\ y>\frac{1}{4}x-2\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186404475 :question/worked-solution "Consider the line $y=x+2.$ Since the line is solid, the inequality is an "or equal to" inequality. Also, since the shaded region lies *below* the line, the inequality is a "less than" inequality. So the corresponding inequality is

$$
y\le x+2.
$$

    

Now consider the line $y=-x+2.$ Since the line is dashed, the inequality is strict. Also, since the shaded region lies *above* the line, the inequality is a "greater than" inequality. So the corresponding inequality is

$$
y>-x+2.
$$

Therefore, the system of inequalities that defines the shaded region is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}y\le x+2 \\ y>-x+2.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186404476 :answer-field/correct "answer-ea85fa77-5fe3-59b1-a642-7a3377ab8ed7" :answer-field/choices ["answer-a6ae492d-6998-592e-aad4-9e4158c3d62a" "answer-8760f28c-314a-5353-a151-1773d06194c2" "answer-d086efec-878a-5d60-959f-69c0d1d6a64c" "answer-ea85fa77-5fe3-59b1-a642-7a3377ab8ed7" "answer-dfc950a4-a4b3-574a-9a32-22ca9de0541d"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a6ae492d-6998-592e-aad4-9e4158c3d62a" :answer/id #uuid "a6ae492d-6998-592e-aad4-9e4158c3d62a" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}y<x+2 \\ y\ge -x+2\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8760f28c-314a-5353-a151-1773d06194c2" :answer/id #uuid "8760f28c-314a-5353-a151-1773d06194c2" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}y>x+2 \\ y\le -x+2\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-d086efec-878a-5d60-959f-69c0d1d6a64c" :answer/id #uuid "d086efec-878a-5d60-959f-69c0d1d6a64c" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}y\ge x+2 \\ y<-x+2\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-ea85fa77-5fe3-59b1-a642-7a3377ab8ed7" :answer/id #uuid "ea85fa77-5fe3-59b1-a642-7a3377ab8ed7" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}y\le x+2 \\ y>-x+2\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-dfc950a4-a4b3-574a-9a32-22ca9de0541d" :answer/id #uuid "dfc950a4-a4b3-574a-9a32-22ca9de0541d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}y\le x+2 \\ y\ge -x+2\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]}]

$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186240596 :answer-field/correct "answer-7c72eb67-dc8d-5199-baad-e8806a1db03d" :answer-field/choices ["answer-3b4fe627-d7c1-50a5-a27e-4f77766ccffc" "answer-1bf1ba90-d97e-56e1-8be0-67555fe8bfec" "answer-7c72eb67-dc8d-5199-baad-e8806a1db03d" "answer-d249a876-1cdc-59b3-9cf5-a76a41e27fb1" "answer-84ffc0a6-3416-5aad-a60b-0475613c9718"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3b4fe627-d7c1-50a5-a27e-4f77766ccffc" :answer/id #uuid "3b4fe627-d7c1-50a5-a27e-4f77766ccffc" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{i,j,k,…,z\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1bf1ba90-d97e-56e1-8be0-67555fe8bfec" :answer/id #uuid "1bf1ba90-d97e-56e1-8be0-67555fe8bfec" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{j,k,l…,z\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-7c72eb67-dc8d-5199-baad-e8806a1db03d" :answer/id #uuid "7c72eb67-dc8d-5199-baad-e8806a1db03d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{k,l,m,…,z\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-d249a876-1cdc-59b3-9cf5-a76a41e27fb1" :answer/id #uuid "d249a876-1cdc-59b3-9cf5-a76a41e27fb1" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{l,m,n…,z\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-84ffc0a6-3416-5aad-a60b-0475613c9718" :answer/id #uuid "84ffc0a6-3416-5aad-a60b-0475613c9718" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{m,n,o…,z\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186399685 :question/worked-solution "Consider the line $x+2y=-8.$ Since the line is solid, the inequality is an "or equal to" inequality. Writing the equation of this line in slope-intercept form, we have

$$
y=-\frac{1}{2}x-4.
$$

Now, since the shaded region lies *above* the line, the inequality is a "greater than" inequality. So the corresponding inequality is

$$
y\ge -\frac{1}{2}x-4,
$$

    

which we can rewrite as

$$
x+2y\ge -8.
$$

Now consider the line $y=\frac{1}{2}x+1.$ Since the line is solid, the inequality is an "or equal to" inequality. Also, since the shaded region lies *below* the line, the inequality is a "less than" inequality. So the corresponding inequality is

$$
y\le \frac{1}{2}x+1.
$$

Therefore, the system of inequalities that defines the shaded region is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+2y\ge -8 \\ y\le \frac{1}{2}x+1.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186399686 :answer-field/correct "answer-e2fad8bd-39bf-566b-87a3-d1e291f8834c" :answer-field/choices ["answer-55750735-57ef-5704-978f-016957530d23" "answer-2ba7e269-52f8-5419-b3c2-ce59a9e64ef4" "answer-e2fad8bd-39bf-566b-87a3-d1e291f8834c" "answer-510522b1-69d4-55a5-928c-930d7659e841" "answer-9cea3798-a1cb-5294-bc97-fc263be948fc"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-55750735-57ef-5704-978f-016957530d23" :answer/id #uuid "55750735-57ef-5704-978f-016957530d23" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}x+2y>-8 \\ y>\frac{1}{2}x+1\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-2ba7e269-52f8-5419-b3c2-ce59a9e64ef4" :answer/id #uuid "2ba7e269-52f8-5419-b3c2-ce59a9e64ef4" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}x+2y\ge -8 \\ y\ge \frac{1}{2}x+1\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-e2fad8bd-39bf-566b-87a3-d1e291f8834c" :answer/id #uuid "e2fad8bd-39bf-566b-87a3-d1e291f8834c" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}x+2y\ge -8 \\ y\le \frac{1}{2}x+1\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-510522b1-69d4-55a5-928c-930d7659e841" :answer/id #uuid "510522b1-69d4-55a5-928c-930d7659e841" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}x+2y\le -8 \\ y\ge \frac{1}{2}x+1\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-9cea3798-a1cb-5294-bc97-fc263be948fc" :answer/id #uuid "9cea3798-a1cb-5294-bc97-fc263be948fc" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}x+2y\le -8 \\ y\le \frac{1}{2}x+1\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186247383 :question/problem "Which expression is missing in the following equation?

$$" :question/worked-solution "To find $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{4}),$ we need to find the number that is located in row $6$ and position $4$ of Pascal's triangle. 

**Important**: When counting the rows and positions in Pascal's triangle, we always start counting from zero! Remember:

- The top row of Pascal's triangle is row $0.$

- The first position of each row (the one of the left) is position number $0.$

The location of $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{4})$ in Pascal's triangle is highlighted below.

$$
\begin{aligned} &  &  &  &  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{0}{0}) \\  &  &  &  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{1}{0}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{1}{1}) \\  &  &  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{0}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{1}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{2}) \\  &  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{0}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{1}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{2}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{3}) \\  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{0}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{1}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{2}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{3}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{4}) \\  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{0}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{1}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{2}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{3}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{4}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{5}) \\  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{0}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{1}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{2}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{3}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{4}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{5}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{6}) \\  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Now, $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{4})$ is the sum of the two closest numbers located in the previous row. So,

$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=1 \\ {x}_{2}=1 \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=7\end{aligned}

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 5 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-5{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=1 \\ {x}_{2}=1 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=1.$ Substituting into the first equation gives 

$$
{x}_{1}-1=1\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2.

Since the system has a solution, we can conclude that $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}.$

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $b$ as a linear combination of ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}:$

$$

$$

$$" :question/worked-solution "To find $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{1}),$ we need to find the number that is located in row $3$ and position $1$ of Pascal's triangle. 

**Important**: When counting the rows and positions in Pascal's triangle, we always start counting from zero! Remember:

- The top row of Pascal's triangle is row $0.$

- The first position of each row (the one of the left) is position number $0.$

The location of $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{1})$ in Pascal's triangle is highlighted below.

$$
\begin{aligned} &  &  &  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{0}{0}) \\  &  &  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{1}{0}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{1}{1}) \\  &  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{0}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{1}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{2}) \\  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{0}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{1}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{2}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{3}) \\  &  &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Now, $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{1})$ is the sum of the two closest numbers located in the previous row. So,

$$

$$" :question/worked-solution "To find $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{2}),$ we need to find the number that is located in row $3$ and position $2$ of Pascal's triangle. 

**Important**: When counting the rows and positions in Pascal's triangle, we always start counting from zero! Remember:

- The top row of Pascal's triangle is row $0.$

- The first position of each row (the one of the left) is position number $0.$

The location of $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{2})$ in Pascal's triangle is highlighted below.

$$
\begin{aligned} &  &  &  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{0}{0}) \\  &  &  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{1}{0}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{1}{1}) \\  &  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{0}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{1}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{2}) \\  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{0}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{1}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{2}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{3}) \\  &  &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Now, $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{2})$ is the sum of the two closest numbers located in the previous row. So,

$$
(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{2})=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{1})+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{2})
$$

Therefore, the missing expression is $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{2}).$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186335645 :answer-field/correct "answer-4f61bb02-7c6b-599e-bcda-28faca2378f8" :answer-field/choices ["answer-7b20281e-3116-5c7a-9362-f88b58a1e766" "answer-3d54b2a8-70b8-57d2-b26c-e1b263ac6824" "answer-809103a8-aba5-597f-b3d9-d4ff88026e05" "answer-a725e35f-5fa7-5d30-a593-8ae1d44e2785" "answer-4f61bb02-7c6b-599e-bcda-28faca2378f8"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-7b20281e-3116-5c7a-9362-f88b58a1e766" :answer/id #uuid "7b20281e-3116-5c7a-9362-f88b58a1e766" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{1}{0})" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3d54b2a8-70b8-57d2-b26c-e1b263ac6824" :answer/id #uuid "3d54b2a8-70b8-57d2-b26c-e1b263ac6824" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{1}{1})" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-809103a8-aba5-597f-b3d9-d4ff88026e05" :answer/id #uuid "809103a8-aba5-597f-b3d9-d4ff88026e05" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{0})" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a725e35f-5fa7-5d30-a593-8ae1d44e2785" :answer/id #uuid "a725e35f-5fa7-5d30-a593-8ae1d44e2785" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{1})" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-4f61bb02-7c6b-599e-bcda-28faca2378f8" :answer/id #uuid "4f61bb02-7c6b-599e-bcda-28faca2378f8" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{2})" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186338838 :question/worked-solution "Remember that the Cartesian (canonical) equation of the straight line that passes through the point $P({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=⟨{v}_{x},{v}_{y},{v}_{z}⟩$, is given by

$$
\frac{x-{x}_{0}}{{v}_{x}}=\frac{y-{y}_{0}}{{v}_{y}}=\frac{z-{z}_{0}}{{v}_{z}}=t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Comparing the above to our given equation

$$
\frac{x-11}{-4}=\frac{y-(-3)}{5}=\frac{z-(-1)}{3},
$$

we find that our line passes through the point $P(11,-3,-1)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨-4,5,3⟩.$ Therefore, its vector equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ -3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations are the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=11-4t \\ y=-3+5t \\ z=-1+3t\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186338687 :answer-field/correct "answer-4b7409a3-17df-5f35-9a98-53b2b56e27b0" :answer-field/choices ["answer-2aad0314-cdde-56d6-9fc9-f1e44fdcf531" "answer-2670e300-5558-54cf-aa24-1fbeb9d684b0" "answer-b720935d-3a6b-53b7-8467-e0328c75249f" "answer-4b7409a3-17df-5f35-9a98-53b2b56e27b0"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-2aad0314-cdde-56d6-9fc9-f1e44fdcf531" :answer/id #uuid "2aad0314-cdde-56d6-9fc9-f1e44fdcf531" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}x=-11-4t \\ y=3+5t \\ z=1+3t\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-2670e300-5558-54cf-aa24-1fbeb9d684b0" :answer/id #uuid "2670e300-5558-54cf-aa24-1fbeb9d684b0" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}x=-4+11t \\ y=5-3t \\ z=3-t\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b720935d-3a6b-53b7-8467-e0328c75249f" :answer/id #uuid "b720935d-3a6b-53b7-8467-e0328c75249f" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}x=-4t \\ y=5t \\ z=3t\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-4b7409a3-17df-5f35-9a98-53b2b56e27b0" :answer/id #uuid "4b7409a3-17df-5f35-9a98-53b2b56e27b0" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}x=11-4t \\ y=-3+5t \\ z=-1+3t\end{aligned}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186351158 :question/problem "Find all of the subsets of $U=\{-\pi ,\pi \}.$" :question/worked-solution "To find every subset of $U,$ we list out every combination of elements within $U.$ 

We can use the following diagram to visualize the process:

Note that we must include the empty set since it is a subset of every set.

By doing this, we get

$$
∅,\{-\pi \},\{\pi \},\{-\pi ,\pi \}.
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186351128 :answer-field/correct "answer-a581296f-1ffd-5680-83b4-0a132fb259d4" :answer-field/choices ["answer-cceb7cd8-d3cb-5022-80c1-91cc18c492dd" "answer-a7e833ed-7b92-5b0e-ac1a-b54703f7a2bf" "answer-d6a266a0-5552-509f-ae6b-32ef2b01771f" "answer-8560767a-af4e-5ac9-984b-0d56ecc22cf9" "answer-a581296f-1ffd-5680-83b4-0a132fb259d4"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-cceb7cd8-d3cb-5022-80c1-91cc18c492dd" :answer/id #uuid "cceb7cd8-d3cb-5022-80c1-91cc18c492dd" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{-\pi \},\{\pi \}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a7e833ed-7b92-5b0e-ac1a-b54703f7a2bf" :answer/id #uuid "a7e833ed-7b92-5b0e-ac1a-b54703f7a2bf" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{-\pi \},\{\pi \},\{-\pi ,\pi \}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-d6a266a0-5552-509f-ae6b-32ef2b01771f" :answer/id #uuid "d6a266a0-5552-509f-ae6b-32ef2b01771f" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "∅,\{-\pi ,\pi \}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8560767a-af4e-5ac9-984b-0d56ecc22cf9" :answer/id #uuid "8560767a-af4e-5ac9-984b-0d56ecc22cf9" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "∅,\{-\pi \},\{\pi \}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a581296f-1ffd-5680-83b4-0a132fb259d4" :answer/id #uuid "a581296f-1ffd-5680-83b4-0a132fb259d4" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "∅,\{-\pi \},\{\pi \},\{-\pi ,\pi \}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186351176 :question/worked-solution "The multiples of $10$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
C=\{10,20,30,40,50,60,70,…\}.
$$

Likewise, multiples of $5$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
D=\{5,10,15,20,25,30,35,40,45,50,55,60,65,70,75,…\}.
$$

Now, $C∖D$ is the *difference* of $C$ and $D,$ which means that we want to find the elements that are in $C$ but *not* in $D.$

The elements of $C$ that are also in $D$ are $10,20,30,40,$ and so on (i.e. multiples of $10$). So, we must remove these elements from $C.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}C∖D & =C-D \\  & =\{10,20,30,40,50,60,70,…\}-\{5,10,15,20,25,30,35,40,45,50,55,60,65,70,75,…\} \\  & =∅.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186351004 :answer-field/choices ["answer-1eee49b7-7d23-57d3-be48-80546786725e" "answer-d54904e8-c3f4-50ab-b94b-312c9c80dbb1" "answer-3656c7be-564a-5dca-b523-f1cf8ca9939f" "answer-e8c1a6ce-e81b-50b5-825e-bab71ce12858"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1eee49b7-7d23-57d3-be48-80546786725e" :answer/id #uuid "1eee49b7-7d23-57d3-be48-80546786725e" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{10,20,30,40,50,60,70,…\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-d54904e8-c3f4-50ab-b94b-312c9c80dbb1" :answer/id #uuid "d54904e8-c3f4-50ab-b94b-312c9c80dbb1" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{15,30,45,60,75,…\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3656c7be-564a-5dca-b523-f1cf8ca9939f" :answer/id #uuid "3656c7be-564a-5dca-b523-f1cf8ca9939f" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{5,10,15,20,25,30,35,40,45,50,55,60,65,70,75,…\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-e8c1a6ce-e81b-50b5-825e-bab71ce12858" :answer/id #uuid "e8c1a6ce-e81b-50b5-825e-bab71ce12858" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{5,15,25,35,45,55,65,75,…\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186351258 :question/problem "If $U=\{1,2,3,…,10\}$ is the universal set and $A=\{2,4,6,8,10\},$ then the complement of $A$ is" :question/worked-solution "The complement of $A,$ denoted $\overset{―}{A},$ consists of every element in the universal set $U$ that is not in the set $A.$

\overset{―}{A}=\{1,3,5,7,9\}.
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186350765 :answer-field/correct "answer-32175474-2a33-5edd-82d1-ca23fe06b582" :answer-field/choices ["answer-8e2a7810-134a-59c6-95e0-9e32883d711d" "answer-5b05c18c-16d7-52fb-815b-13f340ae470d" "answer-32175474-2a33-5edd-82d1-ca23fe06b582" "answer-0ae8da4d-49d1-5d59-b5f2-9ba7fac1a5ce" "answer-62686a45-f9e0-5352-8bd0-280e32a4a7dd"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8e2a7810-134a-59c6-95e0-9e32883d711d" :answer/id #uuid "8e2a7810-134a-59c6-95e0-9e32883d711d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{0,3,6,9\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-5b05c18c-16d7-52fb-815b-13f340ae470d" :answer/id #uuid "5b05c18c-16d7-52fb-815b-13f340ae470d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-32175474-2a33-5edd-82d1-ca23fe06b582" :answer/id #uuid "32175474-2a33-5edd-82d1-ca23fe06b582" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{1,3,5,7,9\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-0ae8da4d-49d1-5d59-b5f2-9ba7fac1a5ce" :answer/id #uuid "0ae8da4d-49d1-5d59-b5f2-9ba7fac1a5ce" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{1,3,6,9\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-62686a45-f9e0-5352-8bd0-280e32a4a7dd" :answer/id #uuid "62686a45-f9e0-5352-8bd0-280e32a4a7dd" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{3,5,7,9\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186351259 :question/problem "If $U=\{-20,-18,-16,-14,…,20\}$ is the universal set and $A=\{-20,-16,-12,-8,…,20\},$ then $\overset{―}{A}=$" :question/worked-solution "The complement of $A,$ denoted $\overset{―}{A},$ consists of every element in the universal set $U$ that is not in the set $A.$

Given the sets $S=\{p,a,s,w,o,r,d\}$ and $T=\{p,o,r,t,e,l\},$ find $T∖S.$" :question/worked-solution "The difference $T∖S$ consists of all the elements that are in $T$ but not $S.$ To represent $T∖S,$ we will shade in all the area that is contained in $T$ but not $S.$

Therefore, the difference is

$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186350742 :answer-field/correct "answer-cde8a77d-917c-5d32-aebb-5d7a0c324a5d" :answer-field/choices ["answer-44d69e04-701b-532a-8660-e10b61e27da0" "answer-c0ebd0cd-50f3-5d9b-b33d-13fa3b3356f9" "answer-6386c1eb-6556-5007-86bd-5b23aac19731" "answer-3e57db84-9532-5a86-b209-39f3021ccc79" "answer-cde8a77d-917c-5d32-aebb-5d7a0c324a5d"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-44d69e04-701b-532a-8660-e10b61e27da0" :answer/id #uuid "44d69e04-701b-532a-8660-e10b61e27da0" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{a,s,w,d\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-c0ebd0cd-50f3-5d9b-b33d-13fa3b3356f9" :answer/id #uuid "c0ebd0cd-50f3-5d9b-b33d-13fa3b3356f9" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{p,a,s,t,e,l\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-6386c1eb-6556-5007-86bd-5b23aac19731" :answer/id #uuid "6386c1eb-6556-5007-86bd-5b23aac19731" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{p,o,r\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3e57db84-9532-5a86-b209-39f3021ccc79" :answer/id #uuid "3e57db84-9532-5a86-b209-39f3021ccc79" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{t,e,l,a,s,w,d\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-cde8a77d-917c-5d32-aebb-5d7a0c324a5d" :answer/id #uuid "cde8a77d-917c-5d32-aebb-5d7a0c324a5d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{t,e,l\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186351367 :question/worked-solution "The multiples of $3$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
A=\{3,6,9,12,15,18,21,24,…\}.
$$

Likewise, multiples of $4$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
B=\{4,8,12,16,20,24,…\}.
$$

Now, $B-A$ is the *difference* of $B$ and $A,$ which means that we want to find the elements that are in $B$ but *not* in $A.$

The elements of $B$ that are also in $A$ are $12,24,$ and so on (i.e. multiples of $12$). So, we must remove these elements from $B.$ Therefore, we have

The universal set $U$ consists of the letters $a$ through $z,$ while the set $Y$ consists of the letters $a$ through $j.$

Now, since the shaded region lies *above* the line, the inequality is a "greater than" inequality. So the corresponding inequality is

$$
y\ge -\frac{1}{2}x-4,
$$

    

which we can rewrite as

$$
x+2y\ge -8.
$$

Now consider the line $y=\frac{1}{2}x+1.$ Since the line is solid, the inequality is an "or equal to" inequality. Also, since the shaded region lies *below* the line, the inequality is a "less than" inequality. So the corresponding inequality is

$$
y\le \frac{1}{2}x+1.
$$

Therefore, the system of inequalities that defines the shaded region is

$$

$$

Now, $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{4})$ is the sum of the two closest numbers located in the previous row. So,

$$
(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{4})=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{3})+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{4})
$$

Therefore, the missing expression is $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{3}).$"] ["answer-fb3123f1-385a-5a7b-84da-6fe907b81043" :answer/id #uuid "fb3123f1-385a-5a7b-84da-6fe907b81043"] function $f(x)$ as

$$
f(x)=(x+2)^{4}(x+5)(x-7).
$$

So we're now solving the inequality $f(x)\ge 0.$

The solutions to the equation $f(x)=0$ are $x=-5,$ $x=-2,$ and $x=7.$ These roots divide the number line into $4$ subintervals:

$$
(-\infty ,-5),\,(-5,-2),\,(-2,7),\,(7,\infty ).
$$

Now, we construct a sign table with the list of the intervals on the top and the list of factors on the left. Filling in the sign table using the usual method, we get the following result:

|  | $(-\infty ,-5)$ | $(-5,-2)$ | $(-2,7)$ | $(7,\infty )$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $(x+2)^{4}$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| $x+5$ | $-$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| $x-7$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| $f(x)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |

Finally, to solve the inequality $f(x)\ge 0,$ we look at the bottom row to determine where $f(x)$ is positive.

From the table, we see that $f(x)$ is positive on the intervals $(-\infty ,-5)$ and $(7,\infty ).$

Therefore, remembering that the roots are also solutions, we conclude that $f(x)\ge 0$ for all $x\in (-\infty ,-5]\cup \{-2\}\cup [7,\infty ).$"] ["answer-54ce1c89-ead7-51f7-8d45-c8b886b66b84" :answer/id #uuid "54ce1c89-ead7-51f7-8d45-c8b886b66b84"] ["answer-54ce1c89-ead7-51f7-8d45-c8b886b66b84" :answer/type :answer.type/math] ["answer-54ce1c89-ead7-51f7-8d45-c8b886b66b84" :answer/value "x\in (-\infty ,-5]\cup \{-2\}\cup [7,\infty )"] ["answer-4c47f54b-e89e-5b4f-8218-dda45e7ee776" :answer/id #uuid "4c47f54b-e89e-5b4f-8218-dda45e7ee776"] ["answer-4c47f54b-e89e-5b4f-8218-dda45e7ee776" :answer/type :answer.type/math] ["answer-4c47f54b-e89e-5b4f-8218-dda45e7ee776" :answer/value "x\in \{-2\}\cup [7,\infty )"] [17592186252925 :answer-field/correct "answer-54ce1c89-ead7-51f7-8d45-c8b886b66b84"] [17592186252925 :answer-field/choices "answer-54ce1c89-ead7-51f7-8d45-c8b886b66b84"] [17592186252925 :answer-field/choices "answer-4c47f54b-e89e-5b4f-8218-dda45e7ee776"] [17592186253275 :question/worked-solution "First, we factor the polynomial on the left-hand side of the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{4}+3{x}^{3}-28{x}^{2} & ={x}^{2}({x}^{2}+3x-28) \\  & ={x}^{2}({x}^{2}+7x-4x-28) \\  & ={x}^{2}(x(x+7)-4(x+7)) \\  & ={x}^{2}(x-4)(x+7)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we define the function $f(x)$ as

$$
f(x)={x}^{2}(x-4)(x+7).
$$

So we're now solving the inequality $f(x)\ge 0.$

The solutions to the equation $f(x)=0$ are $x=-7,$ $x=0,$ and $x=4.$ These roots divide the number line into $4$ subintervals: 

$$
(-\infty ,-7),\,(-7,0),\,(0,4),\,(4,\infty ).
$$

Now, we construct a sign table with the list of the intervals on the top and the list of factors on the left. Filling in the sign table using the usual method, we get the following result:

|  | $(-\infty ,-7)$ | $(-7,0)$ | $(0,4)$ | $(4,\infty )$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x+7$ | $-$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| ${x}^{2}$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| $x-4$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| $f(x)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |

Finally, to solve the inequality $f(x)\ge 0,$ we look at the bottom row to determine where $f(x)$ is positive.

From the table, we see that $f(x)$ is positive on the intervals $(-\infty ,-7),$ and $(4,\infty ).$

Therefore, remembering that the roots are also solutions, we conclude that $f(x)\ge 0$ for all $x\in (-\infty ,-7]\cup \{0\}\cup [4,\infty ).$"] ["answer-30a52b11-8598-5077-8a15-643c9fad9ec2" :answer/id #uuid "30a52b11-8598-5077-8a15-643c9fad9ec2"] ["answer-30a52b11-8598-5077-8a15-643c9fad9ec2" :answer/type :answer.type/math] ["answer-30a52b11-8598-5077-8a15-643c9fad9ec2" :answer/value "x\in (-\infty ,-7]\cup \{0\}"] ["answer-f5cd511b-8452-59e5-b598-ca1eb9dd99c8" :answer/id #uuid "f5cd511b-8452-59e5-b598-ca1eb9dd99c8"] ["answer-f5cd511b-8452-59e5-b598-ca1eb9dd99c8" :answer/type :answer.type/math] ["answer-f5cd511b-8452-59e5-b598-ca1eb9dd99c8" :answer/value "x\in (-\infty ,-7]\cup \{0\}\cup [4,\infty )"] ["answer-fc70ad66-635a-5913-b502-a590c621334d" :answer/id #uuid "fc70ad66-635a-5913-b502-a590c621334d"] ["answer-fc70ad66-635a-5913-b502-a590c621334d" :answer/type :answer.type/math] ["answer-fc70ad66-635a-5913-b502-a590c621334d" :answer/value "x\in \{0\}\cup [4,\infty )"] [17592186253002 :answer-field/correct "answer-f5cd511b-8452-59e5-b598-ca1eb9dd99c8"] [17592186253002 :answer-field/choices "answer-30a52b11-8598-5077-8a15-643c9fad9ec2"] [17592186253002 :answer-field/choices "answer-f5cd511b-8452-59e5-b598-ca1eb9dd99c8"] [17592186253002 :answer-field/choices "answer-fc70ad66-635a-5913-b502-a590c621334d"] [17592186253546 :question/problem "Find all of the subsets of $A=\{x,y,z\}.$"] [17592186253546 :question/worked-solution "To find every subset of $A,$ we list out every combination of elements within $A.$

$$
\frac{x-{x}_{0}}{{v}_{x}}=\frac{y-{y}_{0}}{{v}_{y}}=\frac{z-{z}_{0}}{{v}_{z}}=t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Comparing the above to our given equation

$$
\frac{x-10}{7}=\frac{y-(-8)}{-4}=\frac{z-(-1)}{11},
$$

we find that our line passes through the point $P(10,-8,-1)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨7,-4,11⟩.$ Therefore, its vector equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -8 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -4 \\ 11\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations are the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=10+7t \\ y=-8-4t \\ z=-1+11t\end{aligned}
$$"] ["answer-020acfa4-543c-54b8-8b22-7b878f6d0d45" :answer/id #uuid "020acfa4-543c-54b8-8b22-7b878f6d0d45"] ["answer-020acfa4-543c-54b8-8b22-7b878f6d0d45" :answer/type :answer.type/math] ["answer-020acfa4-543c-54b8-8b22-7b878f6d0d45" :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}x=10+7t \\ y=-4-8t \\ z=-1-11t\end{aligned}"] ["answer-6aeab917-03af-5aaa-807f-606ae765d324" :answer/id #uuid "6aeab917-03af-5aaa-807f-606ae765d324"] ["answer-6aeab917-03af-5aaa-807f-606ae765d324" :answer/type :answer.type/math] ["answer-6aeab917-03af-5aaa-807f-606ae765d324" :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}x=10+7t \\ y=-7-8t \\ z=-1+t\end{aligned}"] ["answer-49fbf7a6-3fac-5080-8363-be5656606e0c" :answer/id #uuid "49fbf7a6-3fac-5080-8363-be5656606e0c"] ["answer-49fbf7a6-3fac-5080-8363-be5656606e0c" :answer/type :answer.type/math] ["answer-49fbf7a6-3fac-5080-8363-be5656606e0c" :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}x=10+7t \\ y=-8-4t \\ z=-1+11t\end{aligned}"] ["answer-9256b135-afaa-56c0-87dd-9ef764465aa3" :answer/id #uuid "9256b135-afaa-56c0-87dd-9ef764465aa3"] ["answer-9256b135-afaa-56c0-87dd-9ef764465aa3" :answer/type :answer.type/math] ["answer-9256b135-afaa-56c0-87dd-9ef764465aa3" :answer/value "\{\begin{aligned}x=10+7t \\ y=8+4t \\ z=-1+11t\end{aligned}"] [17592186262402 :answer-field/correct "answer-49fbf7a6-3fac-5080-8363-be5656606e0c"] [17592186262402 :answer-field/choices "answer-020acfa4-543c-54b8-8b22-7b878f6d0d45"] [17592186262402 :answer-field/choices "answer-6aeab917-03af-5aaa-807f-606ae765d324"] [17592186262402 :answer-field/choices "answer-49fbf7a6-3fac-5080-8363-be5656606e0c"] [17592186262402 :answer-field/choices "answer-9256b135-afaa-56c0-87dd-9ef764465aa3"] [17592186400380 :question/worked-solution "The augmented matrix consists of two parts: the coefficient matrix and the column of constants.

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ -3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

\{\begin{aligned}x=11-4t \\ y=-3+5t \\ z=-1+3t\end{aligned}

$$
C=\{10,20,30,40,50,60,70,…\}.
$$

Likewise, multiples of $5$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
D=\{5,10,15,20,25,30,35,40,45,50,55,60,65,70,75,…\}.
$$

Now, $C∖D$ is the *difference* of $C$ and $D,$ which means that we want to find the elements that are in $C$ but *not* in $D.$

The elements of $C$ that are also in $D$ are $10,20,30,40,$ and so on (i.e. multiples of $10$). So, we must remove these elements from $C.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}C∖D & =C-D \\  & =\{10,20,30,40,50,60,70,…\}-\{5,10,15,20,25,30,35,40,45,50,55,60,65,70,75,…\} \\  & =∅.\end{aligned}
$$"] ["answer-1eee49b7-7d23-57d3-be48-80546786725e" :answer/id #uuid "1eee49b7-7d23-57d3-be48-80546786725e"] ["answer-1eee49b7-7d23-57d3-be48-80546786725e" :answer/type :answer.type/math] ["answer-1eee49b7-7d23-57d3-be48-80546786725e" :answer/value "\{10,20,30,40,50,60,70,…\}"] ["answer-d54904e8-c3f4-50ab-b94b-312c9c80dbb1" :answer/id #uuid "d54904e8-c3f4-50ab-b94b-312c9c80dbb1"] ["answer-d54904e8-c3f4-50ab-b94b-312c9c80dbb1" :answer/type :answer.type/math] ["answer-d54904e8-c3f4-50ab-b94b-312c9c80dbb1" :answer/value "\{15,30,45,60,75,…\}"] ["answer-3656c7be-564a-5dca-b523-f1cf8ca9939f" :answer/id #uuid "3656c7be-564a-5dca-b523-f1cf8ca9939f"] ["answer-3656c7be-564a-5dca-b523-f1cf8ca9939f" :answer/type :answer.type/math] ["answer-3656c7be-564a-5dca-b523-f1cf8ca9939f" :answer/value "\{5,10,15,20,25,30,35,40,45,50,55,60,65,70,75,…\}"] ["answer-e8c1a6ce-e81b-50b5-825e-bab71ce12858" :answer/id #uuid "e8c1a6ce-e81b-50b5-825e-bab71ce12858"] ["answer-e8c1a6ce-e81b-50b5-825e-bab71ce12858" :answer/type :answer.type/math] ["answer-e8c1a6ce-e81b-50b5-825e-bab71ce12858" :answer/value "\{5,15,25,35,45,55,65,75,…\}"] [17592186351004 :answer-field/choices "answer-1eee49b7-7d23-57d3-be48-80546786725e"] [17592186351004 :answer-field/choices "answer-d54904e8-c3f4-50ab-b94b-312c9c80dbb1"] [17592186351004 :answer-field/choices "answer-3656c7be-564a-5dca-b523-f1cf8ca9939f"] [17592186351004 :answer-field/choices "answer-e8c1a6ce-e81b-50b5-825e-bab71ce12858"] [17592186351258 :question/problem "If $U=\{1,2,3,…,10\}$ is the universal set and $A=\{2,4,6,8,10\},$ then the complement of $A$ is"] [17592186351258 :question/worked-solution "The complement of $A,$ denoted $\overset{―}{A},$ consists of every element in the universal set $U$ that is not in the set $A.$

$$

$$

$$

$$

17592186045487 :db/ident :question.difficulty/moderate} :question/problem "Find ${⋃}_{i\in I}{S}_{i}$, given that $I={0,1,2},$ and

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{0}={0},\,{S}_{1}=(0,1),\,{S}_{2}=(0,2).\end{aligned}
$$" :question/worked-solution "The union of a family of indexed sets is the set containing all elements belonging to *at least one* set in the indexed family:

$$
{⋃}_{i\in I}{A}_{i}={x\in U\,:\,x\in {A}_{i}\,\,\text{for at least one }{A}_{i},\,\,i\in I}
$$

where $U$ is a universal set.

Therefore, in our case, we have

"What would be the system of equations for the following augmented matrix?

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 8 & 6 \\ 4 & 1 & -9\end{aligned}]
$$" :question/worked-solution "The augmented matrix consists of two parts: the coefficient matrix and the column of constants.

The coefficient matrix represents the coefficients in the linear system, while the column of constants represents the constants on the right-hand sides of the equations.

Using the variables $x$ and  $y$,  the corresponding system of equations is

$$
{\begin{aligned}0x+8y=6 \\ 4x+y=-9.\end{aligned}
$$

By simplifying, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}8y=6 \\ 4x+y=-9.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186400387 :question/id #uuid "f0c417e1-432e-591b-889d-c01227fedeb7" :question/math-academy-id "q-129133" :knowledge-point/_questions [{:db/id 17592186059769 :knowledge-point/id #uuid $$
[\begin{aligned}0 & -8 & 4 & -\frac{7}{4} \\ 0 & 5 & \frac{2}{3} & 8 \\ \frac{3}{2} & \frac{1}{3} & 4 & 6\end{aligned}]
$$" :question/worked-solution "The augmented matrix consists of two parts: the coefficient matrix and the column of constants.

The coefficient matrix represents the coefficients in the linear system, while the column of constants represents the constants on the right-hand sides of the equations.

Using the variables $x$, $y$, and $z,$ then, the corresponding system of equations is

$$
{\begin{aligned}0x-8y+4z=-\frac{7}{4} \\ 0x+5y+\frac{2}{3}z=8 \\ \frac{3}{2}x+\frac{1}{3}y+4z=6.\end{aligned}
$$

By simplifying, we obtain 

$$
{\begin{aligned}-8y+4z=-\frac{7}{4} \\ 5y+\frac{2}{3}z=8 \\ \frac{3}{2}x+\frac{1}{3}y+4z=6.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186401833 :question/id #uuid "b5cb76d6-8596-56c0-bf91-5764390c6dbb" :question/math-academy-id "q-20362"} {:db/id 17592186409515 :question/id #uuid Which of the following systems of inequalities defines the shaded region shown above?" :question/worked-solution "Consider the line $y=2x+6.$ Since the line is dashed, the inequality is strict. Also, since the shaded region lies *below* the line, the inequality is a "less than" inequality. So the corresponding inequality is

$$
y<2x+6.
$$

    

Now consider the line $y=5.$ Since the line is dashed, the inequality is strict. Also, since the shaded region lies *below* the line, the inequality is a "less than" inequality. So the corresponding inequality is

$$
y<5.
$$

Therefore, the system of inequalities that defines the shaded region is

$$
{\begin{aligned}y<2x+6 \\ y<5.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186404468 :question/id #uuid "66b0d8c5-2487-53cc-b840-b06edcc12d56" :question/math-academy-id "q-90323" :knowledge-point/_questions [{:db/id 17592186110651 :knowledge-point/id #uuid $$

$$

$$
{\begin{aligned}y>x+2 \\ y\ge -x+1.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186404475 :question/id #uuid "3e5e2c49-2afd-5324-972b-43974f8bfdd9" :question/math-academy-id "q-90327" :knowledge-point/_questions [{:db/id 17592186110652 :knowledge-point/id #uuid $$
y\le x+2.
$$

    

Now consider the line $y=-x+2.$ Since the line is dashed, the inequality is strict. Also, since the shaded region lies *above* the line, the inequality is a "greater than" inequality. So the corresponding inequality is

$$
y>-x+2.
$$

Therefore, the system of inequalities that defines the shaded region is

$$
{\begin{aligned}y\le x+2 \\ y>-x+2.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186110653 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186110537 :question/id #uuid "88a7aab5-813a-58e2-a695-8ee72dd4efb1" :question/math-academy-id "e-7964"} :knowledge-point/id Which of the following systems of inequalities defines the shaded region shown above?" :question/worked-solution "Consider the line $x+2y=-8.$ Since the line is solid, the inequality is an "or equal to" inequality. Writing the equation of this line in slope-intercept form, we have

$$
y=-\frac{1}{2}x-4.
$$

Now, since the shaded region lies *above* the line, the inequality is a "greater than" inequality. So the corresponding inequality is

$$
y\ge -\frac{1}{2}x-4,
$$

    

which we can rewrite as

$$
x+2y\ge -8.
$$

Now consider the line $y=\frac{1}{2}x+1.$ Since the line is solid, the inequality is an "or equal to" inequality. Also, since the shaded region lies *below* the line, the inequality is a "less than" inequality. So the corresponding inequality is

$$
y\le \frac{1}{2}x+1.
$$

Therefore, the system of inequalities that defines the shaded region is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+2y\ge -8 \\ y\le \frac{1}{2}x+1.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186404461 :question/id #uuid "262609c0-5557-5285-b43c-f82fdb8825a5" :question/math-academy-id "q-90054" :knowledge-point/_questions [{:db/id 17592186110653 :knowledge-point/id #uuid $$
y=-x+3.
$$

Now, since the shaded region lies *above* the line, the inequality is a "greater than"  inequality. So the corresponding inequality is

$$
y>-x+3,
$$

    

which we can rewrite as

$$
x+y>3.
$$

Now consider the line $y=2x.$ Since the line is dashed, the inequality is strict.  Also, since the shaded region lies *above* the line, the inequality is a "greater than" inequality. So the corresponding inequality is

$$
y>2x.
$$

Therefore, the system of inequalities that defines the shaded region is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+y>3 \\ y>2x.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186110658 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186110290 :question/id #uuid "4b19b389-7d0e-525b-b37f-787e53f5e3b2" :question/math-academy-id "e-1056"} :knowledge-point/id $$" :question/worked-solution "The  $2\times 2$ matrix represents the coefficients of $x$ and $y,$ while the $2\times 1$ column vector on the right-hand side represents the constants of the equations. So, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}10x+25y=15 \\ 12x+3y=-6\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x+5y=3 \\ 4x+y=-2.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}

straight line that passes through the point $P({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=⟨{v}_{x},{v}_{y},{v}_{z}⟩$, is given by

$$
\frac{x-{x}_{0}}{{v}_{x}}=\frac{y-{y}_{0}}{{v}_{y}}=\frac{z-{z}_{0}}{{v}_{z}}=t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Comparing the above to our given equation

$$
\frac{x-10}{7}=\frac{y-(-8)}{-4}=\frac{z-(-1)}{11},
$$

we find that our line passes through the point $P(10,-8,-1)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨7,-4,11⟩.$ Therefore, its vector equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -8 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -4 \\ 11\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations are the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=10+7t \\ y=-8-4t \\ z=-1+11t\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186304796 :question/id #uuid "cf2db5ae-81e4-5762-b815-c025437def46" :question/math-academy-id "q-32936"} {:db/id 17592186304803 :question/id #uuid :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487 :db/ident :question.difficulty/moderate} :question/problem "The vectors ${a}_{1}$, ${a}_{2}$, and $b$ are given below. Determine if $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$ from the decomposition $b={x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}.$

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{aligned}]
$$" :question/worked-solution "We know that $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=1 \\ {x}_{2}=1 \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=7\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 5 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-5{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=1 \\ {x}_{2}=1 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=1.$ Substituting into the first equation gives 

$$
{x}_{1}-1=1\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2.
$$

Since the system has a solution, we can conclude that $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}.$

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $b$ as a linear combination of ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2{a}_{1}+{a}_{2} & =b \\ 2\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=2\cdot 1=2.$"} {:db/id 17592186315058 :question/id #uuid "d123ca06-d8b5-58e1-a29a-b212c006eac8" :question/math-academy-id "q-34115"} {:db/id 17592186315059 :question/id :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045486 :db/ident :question.difficulty/hard} :question/problem "The vectors ${a}_{1}$, ${a}_{2}$, ${a}_{3}$, and $b$ are given below. Determine if $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}$ from the decomposition $b={x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}.$

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 6 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -14 \\ -14\end{aligned}]
$$" :question/worked-solution "We know that $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$, ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 6 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -14 \\ -14\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{3}=6 \\ -3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+6{x}_{3}=-14 \\ -3{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-14\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 6 \\ -3 & 1 & 6 & -14 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 & -14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 & -14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{3}=6 \\ {x}_{2}=4 \\ {x}_{3}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=-2.$ Substituting into the first equation gives 

$$
{x}_{1}-2(-2)=6\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2.
$$

Since the system has a solution, we can conclude that $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}.$

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $b$ as a linear combination of ${a}_{1}$, ${a}_{2}$ and ${a}_{3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2{a}_{1}+4{a}_{2}+(-2){a}_{3} & =b \\ 2\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+4\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+(-2)\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 6 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -14 \\ -14\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}=2\cdot 4\cdot (-2)=-16.$"} {:db/id 17592186342223 :question/id #uuid "b39a9eda-2020-5222-b891-a65118115aa0" :question/math-academy-id "q-74546"} {:db/id $$

$$

Find the parametric equations of the line shown in the figure above." :question/worked-solution "We know that the line passes through the points $P(-1,3,2)$ and $Q(2,4,5).$ Now, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ t \\ 3t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1+3t \\ 3+t \\ 2+3t\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ And finally, the parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-1+3t \\ y=3+t \\ z=2+3t\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186302398 :question/id #uuid "add06203-1905-5fcf-9c44-6a4bc76cf55f" :question/math-academy-id "q-32818"} {:db/id 17592186124501 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id :question.difficulty/hard} :question/problem "Solve the inequality $(x+2)^{4}(x+5)(x-7)\ge 0.$" :question/worked-solution "First, we define the function $f(x)$ as

$$
f(x)=(x+2)^{4}(x+5)(x-7).
$$

So we're now solving the inequality $f(x)\ge 0.$

The solutions to the equation $f(x)=0$ are $x=-5,$ $x=-2,$ and $x=7.$ These roots divide the number line into $4$ subintervals:

$$
(-\infty ,-5),\,(-5,-2),\,(-2,7),\,(7,\infty ).
$$

Now, we construct a sign table with the list of the intervals on the top and the list of factors on the left. Filling in the sign table using the usual method, we get the following result:

|  | $(-\infty ,-5)$ | $(-5,-2)$ | $(-2,7)$ | $(7,\infty )$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $(x+2)^{4}$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| $x+5$ | $-$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| $x-7$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| $f(x)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |

Finally, to solve the inequality $f(x)\ge 0,$ we look at the bottom row to determine where $f(x)$ is positive.

From the table, we see that $f(x)$ is positive on the intervals $(-\infty ,-5)$ and $(7,\infty ).$

Therefore, remembering that the roots are also solutions, we conclude that $f(x)\ge 0$ for all $x\in (-\infty ,-5]\cup {-2}\cup [7,\infty ).$"} {:db/id 17592186292721 :question/id #uuid :question/worked-solution "First, we factor the polynomial on the left-hand side of the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{4}+3{x}^{3}-28{x}^{2} & ={x}^{2}({x}^{2}+3x-28) \\  & ={x}^{2}({x}^{2}+7x-4x-28) \\  & ={x}^{2}(x(x+7)-4(x+7)) \\  & ={x}^{2}(x-4)(x+7)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we define the function $f(x)$ as

$$
f(x)={x}^{2}(x-4)(x+7).
$$

So we're now solving the inequality $f(x)\ge 0.$

The solutions to the equation $f(x)=0$ are $x=-7,$ $x=0,$ and $x=4.$ These roots divide the number line into $4$ subintervals: 

$$
(-\infty ,-7),\,(-7,0),\,(0,4),\,(4,\infty ).
$$

Now, we construct a sign table with the list of the intervals on the top and the list of factors on the left. Filling in the sign table using the usual method, we get the following result:

|  | $(-\infty ,-7)$ | $(-7,0)$ | $(0,4)$ | $(4,\infty )$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x+7$ | $-$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| ${x}^{2}$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| $x-4$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| $f(x)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |

Finally, to solve the inequality $f(x)\ge 0,$ we look at the bottom row to determine where $f(x)$ is positive.

From the table, we see that $f(x)$ is positive on the intervals $(-\infty ,-7),$ and $(4,\infty ).$

Therefore, remembering that the roots are also solutions, we conclude that $f(x)\ge 0$ for all $x\in (-\infty ,-7]\cup {0}\cup [4,\infty ).$"} {:db/id 17592186292722 :question/id #uuid of $10$ greater than $0$ and let $D$  be the the set of all multiples of $5$ greater than $0.$ What is $C∖D?$" :question/worked-solution "The multiples of $10$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
C={10,20,30,40,50,60,70,…}.
$$

Likewise, multiples of $5$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
D={5,10,15,20,25,30,35,40,45,50,55,60,65,70,75,…}.
$$

Now, $C∖D$ is the *difference* of $C$ and $D,$ which means that we want to find the elements that are in $C$ but *not* in $D.$

The elements of $C$ that are also in $D$ are $10,20,30,40,$ and so on (i.e. multiples of $10$). So, we must remove these elements from $C.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}C∖D & =C-D \\  & ={10,20,30,40,50,60,70,…}-{5,10,15,20,25,30,35,40,45,50,55,60,65,70,75,…} \\  & =∅.\end{aligned}

$$
